articles.title: Two Major West Coast Faults May Rupture Together, Study Finds
articles.summary: New research suggests the Cascadia and San Andreas faults can synchronize, with major earthquakes striking minutes or hours apart. Sediment cores show three such events in 1,500 years. If both ruptured today, multiple West Coast cities could face emergencies at once.

articles.title: Black Holes of All Sizes Follow the Same Rule for Launching Jets
articles.summary: A new study finds that black holes — from stellar-mass to supermassive — launch powerful jets at the same critical stage of feeding. Astronomers used tidal disruption events to watch the process unfold. The key threshold is about 2% of the Eddington limit.

articles.title: These Seals Are Doing Oceanography (And They Don't Even Know It)
articles.summary: Oceanographer Lily Dove used sensors on Antarctic seals to study the Southern Ocean. The seals dive deeper than humans, collecting data on temperature and salinity that helps scientists understand climate change.
